# Ajāta Sutta (Iti 43 (It 2.16 PTS It 37))

**ID:** Iti 43 (It 2.16 PTS It 37)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Ajāta Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ajāta Sutta* ("Unborn", Iti 43; PTS It 37) is a concise doctrinal discourse situated in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Its teaching centers on the proclamation that there exists an unborn (*ajāta*), unbecome (*abhūta*), unmade (*akata*), and unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) reality; because this unfabricated dimension exists, an escape from what is born, become, made, and conditioned is possible [Schmidt-Leukel 2006; Notz 2001].

This passage serves as one of the most prominent canonical statements on the nature of *nibbāna* and has played a significant role in Buddhist exegesis and philosophical debate [Schmidt-Leukel 2006; Notz 2001]. In late classical Indian scholasticism, the formula was central to Abhidharma controversies regarding the ontological status of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) [Dhammajoti 2007; Abhidharmakośabhāṣya 2306 p]. Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika masters cited this sūtra alongside related texts to argue that *nirvāṇa* is a truly existent entity (*padārtha*), whereas opponents such as the Sautrāntikas argued that the phrase "there is the unborn" denotes merely the nominal discontinuation or non-arising of conditioned factors (*janmāpravṛtti*) rather than an independent real entity [Dhammajoti 2007; Abhidharmakośabhāṣya 2306 p]. In the Theravāda tradition, Buddhaghosa cited the passage to demonstrate that *nibbāna* is the sufficient condition of spiritual release [Schmidt-Leukel 2006].

Identical or closely matching formulations appear elsewhere in Buddhist literature, most notably in the *Udāna* (Ud 8.3) and in Sanskrit parallels such as the *Udānavarga* (26.21) [Schmidt-Leukel 2006; Svensk Missionstidskrift 2002; Abhidharmakośabhāṣya 2306 p].

**Sources**

- [Schmidt-Leukel 2006] Perry Schmidt-Leukel (ed.), Buddhism, Christianity and the question of creation: Karmic or divine? (2006) — Discussed canonical passage Iti 43 / Ud 8.3, Buddhaghosa's exegesis, and the characterization of nirvāṇa.
- [Svensk Missionstidskrift 2002] Perry Schmidt-Leukel, 'Christian Perceptions of Buddha', Svensk Missionstidskrift (2002) — Noted parallel text occurrence in Udāna 8.3 and Itivuttaka 43.
- [Abhidharmakośabhāṣya 2306 p] Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Detailed Outlines of Ch. 1-9 of the Abhidharmakośabhāṣya — Noted citations of Itivuttaka 43, Udāna 8.3, and Udānavarga 26.21 in Sarvāstivādin-Vaibhāṣika debates against Vasubandhu.
- [Notz 2001] Klaus-Josef Notz, Lexikon des Buddhismus: Grundbegriffe – Traditionen – Praxis (2001) — Described the central statement of the Buddha on nirvāṇa in Iti 43.
- [Dhammajoti 2007] K. L. Dhammajoti, Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma (2007) — Analyzed the citation of the unborn sūtra (cf. Iti 43) in Sarvāstivādin ontological claims versus Sautrāntika nominalist interpretations.
